newsitem.title: USA: Florida's tobacco case still heading for trial - governor.
newsitem.headline: Florida's tobacco case still heading for trial - governor.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles said Friday his state's lawsuit against tobacco companies would proceed toward an August trial until Congress approves a broad agreement on anti-cigarette litgation and regulation.
Chiles hailed the deal among tobacco companies, state attorneys general and health organisations announced earlier Friday but said a final resolution is far from certain.
"Before we celebrate, let's remember that the next few months will be critical. There will be many hurdles this deal must clear in Congress before it's final," Chiles said in a news release.

"The Florida trial team is going forward with Florida's case, and the only resolution to our suit must be through a consent judgment or decree which will remain enforceable by the court here in Florida," Chiles said.

Florida's lawsuit seeks $1.1 billion or more in Medicaid spending. A trial of the case is scheduled for Aug. 4, making it second only to Mississippi's among the 40 state government lawsuits set for trial.
Lawyers for Florida and the tobacco industry in West Palm Beach, Fla., site of the trial court, said they were continuing their preparations for trial. A pretrial hearing is set for Monday.

"Until the governor and attorney general advises me that they are satisfied that all of the conditions have been met, this case will continue," said Robert Montgomery, one of the lead attorneys for Florida.
Montgomery said the case will continue until the tobacco companies come to court and enter into a consent judgment locking in place all the terms in the agreement announced in Washington.
